title: Geo fan-out and unintended variant escalation: post-incident follow-up
creator: Aisha Gomez
description: Summary: During a capacity spike on 2026-02-27, the smart routing policy erroneously escalated requests to an incompatible model variant and triggered a cross-region fan-out loop that amplified load and caused increased error rates and latency for affected customers. This ticket tracks the postmortem actions, ownership, and verification criteria to prevent recurrence.
timeline:
2026-02-27 10:12 UTC - First spike observed in latency/5xx rate for model-family:rw-7b
2026-02-27 10:18 UTC - Automated fallback to variant tagged 'v2-quant' started; initial errors reported
2026-02-27 10:22 UTC - Routing policy continued to route around local capacity and retried to other regions, causing fan-out
2026-02-27 10:35 UTC - Incident declared; manual policy pause and per-customer pinning applied
2026-02-27 11:10 UTC - Traffic stabilized after pausing new policy rollouts and reverting latest policy-engine deploy
2026-02-27 13:00 UTC - Mitigation: temporary circuit-breaker on cross-region failover enabled
2026-03-01 - Initial incident report and analysis published
root_cause: A recent refactor of the routing policy evaluation engine changed the policy precedence ordering and dropped an explicit variant compatibility check. Combined with an unintentional default change to the sticky-route TTL (from 30s to 0s) in the rollout that removed sticky affinity, requests were eligible for immediate cross-region retries. The combination allowed an incompatible variant ('v2-quant') to be selected for some keys, which returned malformed decoding results; that error path triggered retries that bypassed region preferences and caused a rapid fan-out to other regions, pushing them over capacity and creating cascading fallbacks.
mitigation_summary: Short-term: paused the new routing policy, manually pinned high-throughput customers to known-good variants, added a temporary rate-limiter on cross-region failovers. Long-term: reintroduce variant compatibility validation into the policy engine, enforce a non-zero default sticky-route TTL, add circuit-breaker thresholds for cross-region reroutes, and add regression tests and policy linting before policy deploys.
action_items: ENG-52810-A1: Add variant compatibility matrix check in policy evaluator (owner: Ethan Lin, est: 3, due: 2026-03-12)
ENG-52810-A2: Restore sticky-route TTL default to 30s and make configurable via policy (owner: Maya Patel, est: 2, due: 2026-03-15)
ENG-52810-A3: Implement circuit-breaker that prevents >5 cross-region failovers per minute per-model-family (owner: Priya Shah, est: 5, due: 2026-03-22)
ENG-52810-A4: Add integration test in canary harness that simulates incompatible-variant selection and verifies no fan-out (owner: Daniel Brooks, est: 3, due: 2026-03-18)
ENG-52810-A5: Policy deploy gating: require policy lint + canary delta dashboard and a one-click rollback in console (owner: Product/PM: Jordan Reeves, est: 3, due: 2026-03-29)
ENG-52810-A6: Dashboard & alert: add SLI for cross-region retry rate and alert at 1% sustained (owner: Observability team - Alex Ng, est: 2, due: 2026-03-10)
ENG-52810-A7: Run a tabletop with on-call, routing, and runtime teams to rehearse rollback steps (owner: SRE lead - Camila Ruiz, est: 1, due: 2026-03-08)
ENG-52810-A8: Post-deploy verification checklist for policy engine changes documented in Confluence (owner: Ethan Lin, est: 1, due: 2026-03-12)
ENG-52810-A9: Examine older policy-engine changes for similar precedence inversion regressions and file fixes (owner: Tech Debt - Vijay Rao, est: 2, due: 2026-03-20)
ENG-52810-A10: Customer communications follow-up: send root-cause summary to affected customers and include steps taken (owner: CS - Leila Martins, est: 1, due: 2026-03-05)
verification_steps: Unit test coverage for variant compatibility added and passing in CI
End-to-end canary that simulates capacity drop and asserts no cross-region fan-out beyond configured threshold
New dashboard shows cross-region retry rate baseline and alert fires in staging when threshold crossed
Policy lint prevents missing compatibility checks and fails pre-deploy in CI/CD
Post-deploy runbook executed successfully by on-call during controlled canary
notes: Trade-offs discussed: making the variant compatibility check stricter may temporarily block experimental quantized variants during rollout; to reduce developer friction we propose a staged opt-in for experimental tags plus telemetry to measure regressions. Also evaluating whether sticky-route TTL should be customer-configurable per workload vs a global safety default. Action owners should update this ticket as each subtask completes and attach PRs and dashboard screenshots.
review_feedback: PM review (Jordan Reeves): add mandatory customer notification step; SRE (Camila Ruiz): ensure circuit-breaker thresholds configurable by release. Security note: KMS/keys not involved. QA: add a negative-test assert for malformed decoding path.
